versions.label: GS 0.983 (this build)
changes: Chat: the Scene and Theme chat input fields are now multi-line, so you can see long messages instead of one scrolling line. They start one line tall, grow a line at a time as you type and wrap long text, and scroll after 7 lines (6 on phones) while keeping the chat history in view.
Chat keys: on desktop Enter sends and Shift+Enter adds a new line. On phones Enter adds a new line and the Send button sends, and the keyboard stays up after sending.
VR: the taller chat field is drawn wrapped line by line in the VR menu, with the typing ring around it, and the VR keyboard's Enter key still sends.

versions.label: GS 0.982
changes: Environment → Origin rotation (under Camera): turn the scene's origin so the scene lines up with the view you want, using a 2D gizmo of the X/Y/Z axes as seen from the camera. Drag the ball to rotate, drag the outer ring to roll, click or tap an axis end to point that axis straight at you, or type Yaw/Pitch/Roll. Shift or the Snap 15° toggle snaps, and Reset origin undoes it.
The origin rotation is saved in this browser and with the scene, so Save, scene files, Community uploads and share links keep it. Older scenes open unrotated.
The player, the menus and the lights are not rotated. Physics gravity turns with the scene, GLB/glTF/FBX/OBJ exports bake the rotation in, and the AI is told about the rotation only while one is set.
Works with mouse, touch (44px tap targets on phones) and in VR: the gizmo is painted into the VR menu window and the controller ray can drag it.

versions.label: GS 0.981
changes: VR: every window (the menu, the keyboard and the Hide/Show UI button) is now drawn one way, by painting the real page UI with the HTML canvas renderer. The old hand-drawn VR panels (chat, input bar, side panel, Scenes panel, keyboard, status badge) are gone, and the VR menu is the full menu with all its tabs.

VR: all windows share the same size scale, frame, Fixed/Follow anchoring and controller behaviour: an amber ring shows what the ray points at, trigger clicks, trigger-drag or the thumbstick (with locomotion off) scrolls, and pointing at a text field opens the in-scene keyboard with a cyan typing ring.

VR: better contrast. Text, tab labels, buttons, borders, the selected-tab outline and placeholders now meet WCAG AA in the headset (0 of 39 measured pairs fail, down from 19 of 34), and a renderer bug that drew some labels black on dark backgrounds is fixed.
VR: the Lay down / Sit up option is removed from the VR menu. A saved lay-down setting is cleared and the view starts upright.
VR: Chat → Prompt now works in the headset like on desktop: you can edit the prompt with the VR keyboard and Save it, and Reset asks for a second press instead of a pop-up.

versions.label: GS 0.980
changes: Chat has a new Prompt tab next to Scene and Theme. It shows the full default Scene chat prompt, and you can edit it, Save it, Discard unsaved edits or Reset to default. Your edit is kept in this browser and used for Scene chat and community merges; a "Custom prompt active" badge shows while it is on.

A short required technical section (vr-exec blocks, scene globals, floor and facing) is always added after a custom prompt so scene code keeps running. Custom prompts can be up to 40,000 characters. The auto-fix and theme prompts are shown read-only, and in VR the prompt is read-only.

The default prompt has a new photorealistic lighting and materials section: one motivated shadow-casting key light instead of flat, even lighting, weak fill and ambient, RoomEnvironment reflections, ACES tone mapping, physically based intensities and PBR material values, correct colour spaces, and VR performance limits.
GS's built-in lights are named gsDefaultAmbient and gsDefaultKey so scene code can dim or replace them.

versions.label: GS 0.979
changes: The browser tab now reads "GS For Anything" instead of "Claude VR Chat".
Shared scene pages (/e/ and /s/ links) title the tab with the scene name followed by "GS For Anything".
The GitHub repo is renamed to koshkakochka/gsforanything (https://github.com/koshkakochka/gsforanything). Old krossruiz/gs links redirect.

versions.label: GS 0.978
changes: Phones: while you type in the chat box or the code editor, the panel fills the space above the on-screen keyboard, so the text you are typing, the Send button and the newest messages stay in view. The header, tabs, bottom dock, Hide UI and joysticks step aside while the keyboard is up and come back when it closes. Send keeps the keyboard open.
Phones: less crowded controls. Buttons, tabs, menus and checkboxes are at least 44px tall, text boxes use a 16px font so iOS no longer zooms in, and the screen edges and notch are respected.
Phones: the tabs sit in one row you can scroll sideways, and the chat tools moved behind a "+" button next to the chat box.
Phones in landscape: the chat is a full-height column on the left and the bottom dock moves to the right.
Fixed the on-screen joysticks overlapping the bottom dock on phones.
Desktop, tablet and VR layouts are unchanged.

versions.label: GS 0.977
changes: The desktop camera now uses the standard three.js camera controls, picked in the Controls tab: Orbit (the default, rotating around the scene's center at 0,0,0), Map, Trackball, Fly (drag to look) and First person (click the scene to look around with the mouse, Esc to release, WASD or arrows to walk), plus Off. Each mode lists its keys in the Controls tab.
Removed the custom Orbit and Free-roam controls. A saved Orbit choice stays Orbit, Free-roam becomes First person, and Off stays Off.

Keys move the camera unless you are typing in a text field, even after clicking buttons or panels. The on-screen joysticks appear in Fly and First person, and a game controller drives Orbit, Map, Fly and First person.

versions.label: GS 0.976
changes: Orbit now always rotates around the scene's center (0,0,0): on first load, after Clear scene, after loading a scene, and after Reset Camera View or the gamepad View button. Walking with WASD or the left stick in Orbit used to make the camera circle one point while facing another; now it turns around the point it's looking at.

Free-roam has two small on-screen joysticks in the bottom corners. They are thin see-through rings that fade when idle. The left stick moves forward and back (sideways strafes, like the gamepad's left stick) and the right stick looks around. Both work at once on a phone and can be dragged with the mouse on desktop. They only appear in Free-roam (not in VR), and the Controls tab has a checkbox to hide them.

versions.label: GS 0.975
changes: The desktop and phone view now shows everything the VR view shows. Both draw up to 100 m, but on desktop that used to be counted from the camera, which sits behind where you stand in VR (4 m by default, up to 50 m zoomed out), so faraway objects visible in VR could disappear. Desktop now counts from where you'd stand in VR. VR itself is unchanged.

versions.label: GS 0.974
changes: Added Merge scenes to the Community tab: pick two Community scenes (with the 🔀 button on each row or the Merge scenes bar), say how to combine them, and the AI blends their gameplay, controls and assets into a new scene.

You can choose where each part comes from (gameplay, controls, assets, environment and lighting, UI) and write a prompt. Images and other large assets are carried over exactly without being sent to the AI.

The merge never changes either original. The new scene credits both parents, keeps their history, works with Code tab hot reload, and can be refined by chatting and then published or shared like any other scene.

versions.label: GS 0.973
changes: Added a Share tab with a link to the current scene (the same Community share and View-only link) and 3D model export to GLB, glTF, FBX, OBJ and Blender. GLB, glTF and Blender keep the scene's lights. The same buttons are in the VR Scenes panel.
The code window in VR no longer lags: the headset copy of the menu only repaints when something changes (about 9 ms instead of 76 ms per repaint).
VR windows can stay Fixed or Follow your headset (Controls → VR windows, or the button in the VR Environment panel).
Code tab Apply now hot-reloads only the blocks you changed and keeps their state (gs.state, gs.onUpdate). Full reset rebuilds the whole scene.
VR controller triggers, mouse clicks and touch now work on p5 and canvas panels.

Scenes now save the chat and info log that made them. When you publish, you can see what will be shared, and secrets are removed. Reopening a scene brings the chat back as history so you can keep going, and 📜 shows or downloads the full log.

Import existing p5.js sketches onto panels by paste, file, zip, folder or URL, including p5 web editor and OpenProcessing links. Each sketch runs in its own sandbox, is saved with the scene, and can be edited in the Code tab.

versions.label: GS 0.972
changes: Added ammo.js physics to the page. It is on by default, and scenes that need gravity or collisions use it.
Added a Dependencies tab listing THREE.js, ammo.js and p5.js, with a toggle for each library.
Added a 2D / 3D choice in the Environment tab: 2D uses p5.js or a blank canvas, 3D uses THREE.js (the default) or plain WebGL. The AI follows your choice.
Added game controller support (Xbox Series X|S and other USB or Bluetooth pads): sticks move and look, triggers zoom, Y switches camera mode, and generated scenes can read the controller.
Added a changelog for every version to this version list.

versions.label: GS 0.971
changes: Added a Controls tab for the desktop and phone camera: Orbit (the default), Free-roam (WASD to move, mouse to look, Q/E up and down, Shift to go faster) and Off.
Orbit now circles the scene origin from the first load.
Turned off panning in Orbit mode.

versions.label: GS 0.970
changes: Added a dock at the bottom of the screen that holds the Enter VR button and the version button, so they no longer overlap.

versions.label: GS 0.969
changes: Added Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Haiku 5.5, GPT6 Sol and GPT6 Luna to the model dropdown.

versions.label: GS 0.968
changes: Fixed the Community Scenes layout on desktop.

versions.label: GS 0.967
changes: Added the GS version button and version picker.
First numbered build. It includes all earlier work, most recently:
Code editor syntax highlighting, a 360 / HDRI environment option and a desktop WASD fix.
An HTML-in-canvas menu in VR.
GPT6.1 Sol in the model dropdown.
Loading a community scene clears the world first, with a Layer option and no duplicate loads.
The chat window fits on phones, keeps its header inside the visible Safari viewport, and defaults to a see-through panel with a solid border.

note: Newest first. Each entry: { id, label, url, date, changes[] }. url null = this deployment; otherwise a full https URL (Vercel preview, pinned Worker, etc.). changes are shown as the changelog in the version picker.
